meaning: feeling slightly ill or not quite well
literal_translation: sentirse un poco mal, pachucho o indispuesto
example: I stayed home from work because I was feeling a bit under the weather.
origin: Often linked to sailors sheltering below deck in rough weather; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be standing outside in the rain
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning, not the idiomatic one
The idiom refers to health, not money or social status

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be in charge of the weather
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with controlling weather; it describes how a person feels

explanation: 'Under the weather' means feeling slightly ill or unwell. It is informal and common in everyday speech, especially when someone is not seriously sick.
